newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar called to open flat to 0.05 lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar called to open flat to 0.05 lower.

text.p: CSCE world sugar was called to open unchanged to 0.05 cent lower Thursday on further speculative liquidation of the May contract, dealers said.
The last trading day for the front month is April 30.
Wednesday, May settled 0.18 cent lower at 10.95 cents a lb after trading from 11.10 to 10.87. Most-active July fell 0.16 to 10.85, with the rest finishing 0.11 to 0.05 weaker.
Volume was estimated at a brisk 44,599 lots.
Spot May is expected to find support between 10.90 and 10.80 cents.
In fundamental news, China bought 15,000 tonnes of Thai raw sugar for prompt shipment, trading sources said.
Czarnikow Sugar said India may need to boost imports in 1997/98 due to an anticipated dip in production, but provided no estimate of India's potential requirements.
Thailand's white sugar exports are expected to reach 1.2 million tonnes, down from prior estimates of up to 1.35 million tonnes.
And sugar cane production in Brazil could climb to 287 million tonnes in 1996/97 if the north north-east season (NNE) continues until the end of May, Czarnikow said.

LIFFE white sugar futures were tightly mixed early Thursday amid thin volume, as players awaited the New York open. At 0845 EDT/1345 GMT, August was unchanged at $307.00, while the outer months stood $0.20 higher to down $0.80.
((-- S Rostler New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1640))
